description: Samosas are a beloved Pakistani appetizer, featuring a crispy, flaky pastry shell filled with a savory mixture of spiced potatoes, peas, and sometimes minced meat. These golden-fried triangles are a staple at gatherings and tea-time, offering a burst of aromatic flavors with every bite. Enjoy this classic snack with your favorite chutney for an authentic taste of Pakistan.

ingredients.notes: for dough, plus more for frying

instructions.title: Prepare the Samosa Dough
instructions.text: In a large bowl, combine all-purpose flour, salt, ajwain, and ghee or oil. Rub the ghee into the flour until it resembles breadcrumbs. Gradually add water, kneading until you form a firm, smooth dough. Cover and let it rest for at least 20 minutes.

instructions.title: Cook the Samosa Filling
instructions.text: Heat 2 tablespoons of oil in a pan. Add chopped onions and sauté until translucent. Add ginger-garlic paste and green chilies, cooking for another minute. Stir in coriander powder, cumin powder, red chili powder, turmeric, and garam masala. Cook for 30 seconds until fragrant.

instructions.title: Combine Filling Ingredients
instructions.text: Add the boiled and mashed potatoes and green peas to the spiced mixture in the pan. Mix well, ensuring all ingredients are evenly coated. Cook for 5-7 minutes, stirring occasionally, until the flavors meld. Stir in amchur powder (if using) and fresh coriander leaves. Let the filling cool completely.

instructions.title: Shape the Samosas
instructions.text: Divide the dough into equal small balls. Roll each ball into an oval shape, then cut it in half to create two semi-circles. Take one semi-circle, wet the straight edge with water, and fold it into a cone shape, pressing the seam firmly to seal. Fill the cone with the cooled potato mixture.

instructions.title: Seal the Samosas
instructions.text: Wet the open edges of the filled cone with water. Bring the edges together and press firmly to seal, creating the classic triangular samosa shape. Ensure there are no gaps to prevent the filling from coming out during frying. Repeat with the remaining dough and filling.

instructions.title: Fry the Samosas
instructions.text: Heat oil for deep frying in a karahi or deep pan over medium-low heat. The oil should not be too hot, as this will prevent the crust from becoming crispy. Gently place a few samosas into the hot oil, ensuring not to overcrowd the pan. Fry until golden brown and crispy on all sides, turning occasionally. This usually takes about 8-10 minutes per batch. Remove with a slotted spoon and drain excess oil on paper towels. Serve hot.

tips: For the crispiest Samosas, make sure your dough is firm and rested well. The addition of ghee or oil in the dough is crucial for flakiness.
Always fry Samosas on medium-low heat. If the oil is too hot, the pastry will brown quickly on the outside but remain raw inside.
Ensure your Samosa filling is completely cooled before filling the dough. Warm filling can make the dough soggy and difficult to seal, leading to breakage during frying.
article:
Few appetizers evoke the same warmth, comfort, and culinary delight as the humble samosa. A beloved snack across the globe, it holds a particularly special place in Pakistani cuisine. More than just a fried pastry, it's a staple at tea times, a festive treat during Eid, and an essential part of Iftar during Ramadan. Crispy on the outside, bursting with a savory, spiced filling on the inside, a perfectly made Pakistani samosa is an experience in itself. If you've ever dreamt of recreating that magic in your own kitchen, you're in the right place. This comprehensive guide will walk you through mastering the authentic Pakistani samosa, from kneading the perfect dough to achieving that irresistible golden crisp.

## What is a Samosa?
At its heart, a samosa is a triangular, savory pastry, deep-fried or baked until golden brown. While its exact origins are ancient, tracing back centuries to Central Asia, it became deeply embedded in the Indian subcontinent's culinary traditions. In Pakistan, samosas are typically filled with a spiced mixture of potatoes and peas (aloo samosa) or finely minced meat (keema samosa), often lamb or beef. The distinctive triangular shape is not just for aesthetics; it perfectly encases the generous filling. What sets Pakistani samosas apart is often the robust blend of spices – cumin, coriander, garam masala, and chili – that creates an unforgettable, addictive flavor profile.

## Why You'll Love This Pakistani Samosa Recipe
There’s a unique charm to homemade samosas that store-bought versions often can’t replicate. This particular Pakistani samosa recipe emphasizes fresh ingredients and a balanced spice blend, ensuring an authentic taste that will transport you straight to the bustling streets of Lahore or Karachi. You’ll love the satisfaction of creating these culinary gems from scratch, knowing exactly what goes into each bite. The dough, when prepared correctly, yields a crisp, flaky shell that shatters delightfully with every crunch, perfectly complementing the rich, aromatic filling. This approachable samosa recipe empowers you to bring a piece of Pakistan's rich culinary heritage to your table, impressing family and friends alike.

## Ingredients for Authentic Samosa
Crafting the perfect samosa begins with selecting the right ingredients. For the Dough: You’ll need all-purpose flour, a pinch of salt, carom seeds (ajwain) for a distinctive aroma and digestive aid, and oil or ghee for crispiness and tenderness. Lukewarm water will bring it all together. For the Potato Filling (Aloo Samosa): The stars are boiled and mashed potatoes, green peas (fresh or frozen), finely chopped onion, and fresh green chilies for a kick. The spice blend is crucial: ground cumin, coriander powder, turmeric, red chili powder, garam masala, and dried fenugreek leaves (kasoori methi) for an earthy depth. Fresh ginger and garlic paste add an aromatic foundation. A squeeze of lemon juice or a sprinkle of amchur (dried mango powder) provides a tangy finish. For Keema Samosa: Substitute potatoes with finely minced beef or lamb, ensuring it's lean, and adjust spices accordingly.

## How to Make Samosa: Step-by-Step Guide
Embarking on this culinary journey to create the perfect Pakistani samosa recipe is incredibly rewarding.
1.  **Prepare the Dough:** In a large bowl, combine flour, salt, and ajwain. Rub in the oil or ghee until the mixture resembles coarse crumbs. Gradually add lukewarm water, kneading until you have a firm, smooth, and non-sticky dough. Cover and let it rest for at least 30 minutes. This resting period is vital for a tender, pliable dough.
2.  **Make the Filling:** If making aloo samosas, heat a little oil in a pan, sauté onions until translucent, then add ginger-garlic paste and green chilies. Add all the dry spices and cook for a minute until fragrant. Stir in the mashed potatoes and green peas, mixing well to combine the spices evenly. Cook for a few minutes, then remove from heat, stir in fresh coriander and lemon juice. Let it cool completely. For keema, brown the mince, drain fat, then add spices and cook until done.
3.  **Assemble the Samosas:** Divide the rested dough into small, equal portions. Roll each portion into an oval shape. Cut the oval in half. Take one half, moisten the straight edge with water, and form a cone shape by overlapping the edges. Press firmly to seal.
4.  **Fill and Seal:** Spoon a generous amount of the cooled filling into the cone. Moisten the open edges of the cone with water and gently pinch them together to form the characteristic triangular samosa shape. Ensure a tight seal to prevent the filling from escaping during frying.
5.  **Fry the Samosas:** Heat oil in a deep pan or wok over medium heat. The oil should be hot enough to sizzle when a small piece of dough is dropped in, but not smoking. Carefully lower the samosas into the hot oil, frying in batches to avoid overcrowding. Fry until they are golden brown and crispy on all sides, turning occasionally. This usually takes about 8-10 minutes per batch. Remove with a slotted spoon and drain on paper towels.

## Tips for Perfect Crispy Samosas
Achieving that coveted crispiness is key to a truly satisfying samosa. Firstly, ensure your dough is firm and not too soft; a stiffer dough yields a flakier crust.
